title: Flag-Based Spinlock without Compiler/Memory Barriers
pattern: Synchronizing shutdown or loop termination in parallel threads using standard shared flag writes and reads without atomic/volatile primitives or compiler barriers.
why_bad: The compiler may optimize and fuse consecutive stores or loads, or reorder writes across loops, resulting in infinite lockups or thread starvation.
detection: A tight `while` loop that polls a standard, non-atomic boolean or integer variable modified by another thread without volatile annotations or memory barriers.
counterexample: Spinning on an atomic variable (`std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool` in Rust) with explicit memory ordering constraints.
fix: Wrap shared flags in atomic primitives (`std::sync::atomic` in Rust) or enforce ordering via explicit memory barriers (`smp_mb()`).
source: Paul E. McKenney, *Is Parallel Programming Hard...*, Listing 4.19 / passage [4, 5, 299].
